reasoning.Student A:
My goal is to maximize my chances of getting into the best school possible according to my preferences: w > z > x > y.

School w is my top choice and I have the highest priority (1) there. This is great.

School z is my second choice, but I only have priority 2 there.

School x is my third choice and I have priority 2 there.

School y is my last choice, but I have the highest priority (1) there.

Given the information that most applicants favor y > x > w > z, it seems likely that w will be competitive, but I have the highest priority there, so I should be in a good position.

I will stick to my true preference order. It is important to rank truthfully because rejections only redirect, never eliminate. Being rejected from a school I ranked highly does NOT hurt my chances at schools ranked lower.
